links.outcome: Rate of choosing 'I don't know or cannot answer' on unanswerable questions
links.effect: Of 162 unanswerable questions, Jev chose the 'I don't know' option for 10.5% (GPT-6 Sol, 8.6%), so both models rarely deferred.
links.quote: Of the 162 questions whose correct answer was "I don't know or cannot answer", Jev chose that option for 10.5% (GPT-6 Sol, 8.6%).

links.outcome: Calibration and confidence-accuracy relationship of model probabilities on MetaMedQA
links.effect: Jev ECE 0.063 vs 0.146 for GPT-6 Sol; Jev answers with p>=0.9 (52.9% of questions) were 93.4% accurate, but GPT-6 Sol matched that accuracy at similar coverage. On DiagnosisArena-MCQ, AUROC 0.645 vs 0.768.
links.quote: On MetaMedQA, Jev's probabilities were the best calibrated (expected calibration error 0.063 vs 0.146), and its answers with a probability of at least 0.9 (52.9% of questions) were 93.4% accurate, but GPT-6 Sol was as accurate when it accepted a similar proportion of questions.

unlisted_practices: selective prediction using probability thresholds to abstain on low-confidence answers

screen.reason: Evaluates a non-generative classification/probability model (Jev) alongside GPT-6 on standard medical question-answering and diagnostic benchmarks without evaluating an implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
